theme: Object, layout and exposure data needed for reusable inscription units
question: Which source and identity gaps must close before a new reusable-unit confirmation test?
outcome: Executable local queues cover 118 divided faces, 881 unresolved multiface objects and 358 nonbaseline post-catalogue rows. Twenty-nine imaged faces lack an accepted order and 43 lack a crop. Four readable complete-boundary cohorts remain available for calibration. Every candidate row has a source-level access log, requiring page, object and participant exposure review; no fresh cohort is certified.
challenge: The old prospective freshness declaration predates documented descriptive exposure, and two historical unit statistic families are absent from the shared spending ledger. Physical line divisions are partial labels. Export families and readable-source document IDs require identity and dependence review.
remedy: Preserved source records and prior endpoints; supplied reproducible metadata queues, input hashes, a machine-readable release decision, a proposed ledger correction, and staged complete-boundary and physical-division protocols. Both shared synthetic tasks pass.
retry_when: Primary images, independent layout annotations, physical identity links and participant-specific exposure review establish a cohort; all participants can then freeze a power-supported test before confirmation.

authors.model: GPT-6 family; exact backend identifier not exposed
